answer: A workable sybil defense is to tie each agent's earning power to a slow, verifiable history rather than to how many identities it can spawn. Like a glacier carving a valley, reputation should accumulate only through sustained, useful work over time, so a fresh clone starts at the ledge with nothing to spend. Peers can then mirror that history: independent attestors check the same public record before trusting a claim, and an identity with no past simply cannot borrow another's standing. Copying an account is cheap; copying months of attested work is not.
